clue.text: Hot dish, then cold, very cold

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a metal bowl
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A menu note: something spicy followed by something chilled, with a remark on how chilly it is.
explanation.walkthrough: BALTIC as an adjective for bitterly cold weather is informal British slang, especially in Scotland and the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: In colloquial British usage weather that is freezing is described as Baltic, after the icy northern sea.

clue.text: Hail in a part of Orkney

parts.note: Hoy is one of the islands of the Orkney archipelago off northern Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone is caught in a hailstorm on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like the weather, fitting the puzzle's theme, but it is the verb meaning to call out to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the sailor's greeting used to call to a ship or person, so it is a way to hail them.

clue.text: After torrential sleet cloak glass

indicators.note: the cloak word is placed after the jumbled weather word in the answer
falling in torrents suggests the letters of the word are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: a cope is a long cloak worn by a priest

explanation.surface: After a downpour of sleet, someone wraps themselves in a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torrential' signals the shuffle and 'After' puts the cloak second; 'sleet' and 'glass' look like weather words, but glass here is an optical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass is an old name for a telescope or spyglass, as in a sailor's glass.

clue.text: Sky feature about Irish sport succeeded

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
RU is rugby union
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Something in the sky hovers over an Irish game that went well.
explanation.definitionFit: Cirrus is a high, wispy type of cloud, a familiar feature of the sky.

clue.text: Independent female stops near turbines

indicators.note: to stop something up is to plug it, so these pieces sit inside the other word

parts.note: warm means near, as in the children's guessing game

explanation.surface: A woman of independent mind halts close to some wind turbines.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm is a group of turbines generating electricity, so the collection stands for the whole installation.

clue.text: Expected conditions to endure for English actors

parts.note: to weather a storm is to endure it
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Performers from England must put up with predictable working conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast tells you the atmospheric conditions to expect over the coming days.

clue.text: Pearly king no use working with chartered accountant

indicators.note: working here means in motion and being reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Pearly King, a costumed London charity figure, finds no use for his accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London costermongers in button-covered costumes; 'Pearly king' is split, the first word being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacreous means made of or like nacre, mother-of-pearl, so it describes a pearly lustre (also a type of cloud).

clue.text: US poet improved briefly in paper

indicators.note: the shortened word sits within the newspaper abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: rose means improved, as prices or spirits rise

explanation.surface: An American poet's reputation grew a little in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Frost was an American poet known for poems such as 'The Road Not Taken'.

clue.text: According to some, bank transferred parts

indicators.note: parts in the sense of separates, so the outer word is split to take the other inside

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
ported means carried or transferred, as software is ported

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a bank moved some of its parts elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportedly means as people say or claim, i.e. according to the accounts of others.

clue.text: Leave a large group of old boozers about to invade part of pitch

parts.note: to go is to leave
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

indicators.note: invading means moving into, so the short word goes inside the group's initials

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group of former heavy drinkers
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A crowd of ageing drinkers are told to leave before storming the football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The goal area is the small box marked in front of the goal on a football field.

clue.text: Dispense with pony on leaving with white horses

parts.note: to chop something is to cut or get rid of it

indicators.note: leaving says the word before it departs from the animal's name

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of a pony as they set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white horses' are not animals but waves breaking with white crests on a rough sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A choppy sea is broken by many small waves, the whitecaps sailors call white horses.

clue.text: A little French cash wife's kept in the back of Cornwall?

parts.note: a sou was an old French coin of low value

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the letter is placed within

parts.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so the two words give this

explanation.surface: A wife hides a few French coins at the back of a Cornish house.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-west tip; the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall lies in the far south-west of England, so something belonging to it is south-western.

clue.text: Praises temperature sustained by unit's cold shower

indicators.note: in a down clue being held up by means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: hails means praises or acclaims
one's: a unit is one, plus the possessive

explanation.surface: Praise keeps a unit's temperature up, despite a chilly shower.
explanation.definitionFit: Hailstones are pellets of ice falling from the sky, literally a shower of something cold.

clue.text: Ring round head appearing in encephalogram

indicators.note: the answer is seen appearing in the letters of the long medical word

explanation.surface: A circle around the head shows up on a brain scan.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light around a saint's head; it is also a ring around the sun or moon.

clue.text: Made up name in erudite broadcast

indicators.note: the single letter is placed in the middle of the rearranged word
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A name was invented for a scholarly radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ERUDITE into REUITED, and 'in' puts N among its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up after a quarrel is to be reconciled, so people who made up are reunited.

clue.text: Downing Street leader's about to pursue German girl

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the girl's name comes first

parts.note: Inge is a German girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one, and number one is the leader
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister of Downing Street is about to chase a German girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downing Street' is the Prime Minister's London address, but 'Downing' alone is the definition, meaning swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To down a drink is to swallow it, and ingestion is the act of swallowing food or drink.

clue.text: Spooner's cleverly ignoring old eastern riposte

indicators.note: done cleverly means rearranged in an ingenious way, so the letters are reworked
ignoring means leaving out, so one letter is dropped from the name

explanation.surface: Spooner, the famously muddled speaker, cleverly gives a retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' looks like a Spoonerism signal but is just fodder: 'ignoring old' drops an O and 'cleverly' rearranges SPNERS into RESPONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick reply, and a response is any answer or reply.

clue.text: Change, say, then ring one's closest friend

parts.note: to alter is to change
e.g. means for example, as does say
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Instructions for a phone call: alter something, then ring someone's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, and by extension an intimate friend who is like another self.

clue.text: Greek doctor doesn't finish The Tempest

indicators.note: not finishing means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Galen was an ancient Greek physician

explanation.surface: A Greek physician fails to get to the end of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tempest' reads as Shakespeare's play, but tempest is just a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm with strong winds, essentially a gale.

clue.text: Every so often trips by girl matter

indicators.note: every so often means taking letters at intervals, here every other letter

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl occasionally trips over, which matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is the material of which living bodies are made, so organic matter.

clue.text: This compares different sources of interference

indicators.note: made different means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comparison claims to show different causes of disruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmospherics are electrical disturbances in the air that cause crackling noise on radio reception.

clue.text: Transmitting old northern song

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A radio station broadcasts an old folk song from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being broadcast, i.e. transmitted live.

clue.text: Drops first-class navy trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the navy letters take the other piece inside

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: The navy abandons its smart trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is the verb meaning pockets, not the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is water falling in drops, so drops stands for the whole downpour.

clue.text: One way to carry goods across India, unsuccessfully?

indicators.note: the van phrase stretches across the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: goods can be carried in a van
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Goods are trucked across India, though the trip seems pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort made in vain achieves nothing, i.e. is without success.

clue.text: A carnival bar opening during summer

indicators.note: bar means except, so the opening letter is excluded

parts.note: a carnival is a festival

explanation.surface: A bar opens during a summer carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub opening, but it means excluding, so FESTIVAL loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aestival means relating to or occurring in the summer season, from Latin aestas.

clue.text: European books bound to keep one inside wanting more

indicators.note: the built-up word goes inside the outer pair of abbreviations

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the number goes inside

parts.note: bound to means sure to
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A European keeps buying books and still wants more.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient means hungry or greedy, so always craving more.

clue.text: It causes climatic changes in '09, westbound around Lima

indicators.note: the reversed figures go around the phonetic letter
going west in an across clue means reading right to left

parts.note: zero is O and nine is NINE
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A weather report: in 2009 something heading west round Peru's capital changed the climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westbound' reverses ONINE to ENINO and 'around' wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño is the periodic warming of the Pacific off South America, which disrupts weather worldwide.
